## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Strait of Hormuz Shipping Attacks Hit Record Pace; 30+ Incidents in October, Highest Since Iran War Began

Attacks on merchant vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz have escalated to their highest levels since the conflict with Iran began. Between November 20 and 22, UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) issued three separate attack warnings for tankers in the waterway, with one tanker struck by an unidentified projectile on its port bow at 1500 UTC on November 20, triggering a fire approximately 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. October saw over 30 attack incidents in the region—the highest monthly count since the war's start—with 22 more recorded so far in November. The Joint Maritime Information Center rates the threat level as SEVERE, warning that further deliberate attacks are highly likely.

**Why it matters.** The Strait of Hormuz is the critical passage for roughly 20 percent of global crude oil exports, and India depends on Persian Gulf oil imports for roughly 70 percent of its demand. Any sustained supply disruption ripples directly through downstream sectors: energy prices spike, shipping insurance premiums climb, and power generation costs spike. For a consulting analyst or quant researcher tracking macro tail risks, this is a tier-one watch item. The attacks are also fragmenting maritime insurance and shifting shipping routes, which reorders the cost structure for anyone managing global supply chains or modeling energy complex dynamics.

**Action.** Monitor UKMTO daily advisories for attack frequency trends; cross-check against JMIC severity ratings. Flag if monthly attack counts exceed 40 (a potential tipping point for insurer withdrawal or rerouting cascades). Watch crude Brent futures and shipping ETFs like DCSA for the market's repricing. If you consult in energy or logistics, escalate internal scenarios for 15–30 percent sustained supply tightening, and game out the India-exposed sectors (refiners, shipping lines, power utilities, fertilizer makers who rely on oil feedstock).

*Sources: [cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/22/middleeast/hormuz-attacks-highest-levels-iran-war-intl) · [gcaptain.com](https://gcaptain.com/another-tanker-hit-in-strait-of-hormuz-as-maritime-attacks-surge-worldwide/) · [maritime-executive.com](https://maritime-executive.com/article/two-more-tankers-hit-off-oman-as-houthis-threaten-saudi-red-sea-ports/)*

### Trump and Putin Meet in Shenzhen with Xi Present; Ukraine Diplomacy Unfolds Amid Renewed Attacks

Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held talks in Shenzhen, China on November 19, 2026, with Xi Jinping present, in a trilateral meeting that brought Ukraine directly onto the agenda despite initial US signals to the contrary. Separately, US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrived in Kyiv for a second round of direct diplomacy, while Russia launched over 400 drones and 110 missiles across Ukraine overnight, inflicting at least 15 casualties in the Kyiv region alone. Russia-Ukraine negotiations concluded with a prisoner exchange—both sides releasing and receiving combatants—but produced no visible breakthrough toward a political settlement.

**Why it matters.** The meeting signals a potential realignment of great-power competition over Europe's future, with US-China coordination on the Ukraine question moving from hypothetical to negotiating reality. For a technologist or quant tracking geopolitical regimes, this matters because a US-brokered Ukraine settlement would reshape NATO's posture, defense spending trajectories, and semiconductor export controls—all first-order inputs to tech valuations and supply-chain duration models. India's own strategic hedging (balancing US, Russia, and China partnerships) hinges on how this settlement unfolds; a rushed or asymmetric deal could reset expectations for who India can rely on for military tech, energy trade, and capital. The scale of overnight Russian firepower—400+ drone sorties—also hints at escalating asymmetric tactics that could drag the conflict longer.

**Action.** Bookmark the latest reports from US Treasury on new Russia sanctions or carve-outs; watch for shifts in US semiconductor export controls toward China (downstream chipmakers will reprice). If managing a fund or prop book, track the VIX term structure and implied European geopolitical risk premia. For India-exposed strategies, monitor whether the US negotiating push tilts toward NATO expansion or instead toward a neutral buffer-state model—each assumption spawns different long-duration plays in Indian defense contractors, state-backed funds, and rupee forwards.

*Sources: [nbcnews.com](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/russia-ukraine-news) · [justsecurity.org](https://justsecurity.org/165610/early-edition-november-23-2026/) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/tag/ukraine-russia-crisis/)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Gemini 4 agent teams discover cheaper quantum algorithms, all results formally verified in Lean

DeepMind announced November 23 that multi-agent teams running Gemini 4 optimized quantum algorithms for five problems—inertial confinement fusion, cytochrome P450 simulation, photochemical reactions, state loading (arcsin), and Grover search. Each discovered circuit passed formal verification in the Lean theorem prover. Fusion algorithms cost dropped 11.8x with error-corrected qubit requirement falling from 5,650 to 4,338; chemistry gains ranged 2.5x to 8x; arcsin achieved 290x speedup on a hardware-agnostic level.

**Why it matters.** This demonstrates agentic systems excelling at constrained search over structured problem spaces where formal verification closes the trust gap. For quantum engineers, it means classical circuit optimization bottlenecks may now compress timelines for near-term quantum utility. For infrastructure teams building agent frameworks, it validates multi-agent reasoning loops capable of discovering non-obvious algorithms then proving them correct—a pattern applicable beyond quantum to chip design, cryptography, and mathematical discovery.

**Action.** Check the open-source circuits and problem specs on DeepMind's GitHub. If you're shipping agentic reasoning, audit whether your loop includes a verification step (automated theorem proving, constraint satisfaction, or formal property checking) rather than trusting agent-generated output by default. Run the arxiv paper (posted Nov 6, revised after announcement) to understand how the agent teams were prompted and constrained.

*Sources: [thenextweb.com](https://thenextweb.com/news/google-deepmind-gemini-agents-quantum-algorithms-lean) · [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/google-deepmind-agent-teams-discover-lean-verified-quantum-algorithms/) · [madrobot.blog](https://madrobot.blog/2026/11/23/deepmind-ai-agents-quantum-algorithms-lean-proofs/)*

### Anthropic launches Claude Ship—agentic PR review and fixes with token-metered approvals

Anthropic released Claude Ship on November 23, bundling Code Review (generally available), PR Steward (beta), and Claude Approvals (beta) for GitHub repositories. PR Steward detects failing checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback, then pushes fixes with explanatory comments—developers steer it via @claude comments. Claude Approvals applies a team-written policy file to auto-approve routine PRs. Both run in a cloud session; pricing is token-metered with configurable spend caps per organization.

**Why it matters.** Claude Ship shifts code review from async bottleneck to tight agent-human loop. For teams using Claude in their workflows, it personalizes approval policies (not vendor-mandated) while guaranteeing each fix attempt is logged and reversible. For platforms monitoring agentic adoption, it's proof that code-change agents work best when agents cannot unilaterally merge—the agent proposes, humans retain final gate. Self-reported gains (2x merged PRs, 40% fewer reverts) suggest measurable friction reduction on larger teams if reproducible.

**Action.** If you operate a monorepo or high-merge-volume team, write a Claude Approvals policy file (YAML format, documented in Claude Code docs) and pilot PR Steward in observe-only mode before making approvals a required check. Measure your actual merge velocity and revert rate before and after to validate claimed 2x gains. Watch for edge cases where policy files conflict or agent-generated fixes mask deeper issues.

*Sources: [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/anthropic-launches-claude-ship-to-review-fix-and-approve-prs/) · [xda-developers.com](https://www.xda-developers.com/anthropics-new-claude-ship-feature-lets-your-assistant-review-fix-approve-pull-requests/) · [code.claude.com](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/pr-steward)*

## 🇮🇳 India

### CortexSpark Ventures Launches ₹1,000 Crore Deeptech Fund With SEBI Approval

CortexSpark Ventures received SEBI regulatory approval on November 24, 2026 for a dedicated ₹1,000 crore deeptech venture fund. The fund targets frontier technologies including artificial intelligence, semiconductor design, robotics, and other hardware-first companies typically starved for patient capital. This is the first major deeptech-focused deployment mechanism approved in India's startup ecosystem this quarter.

**Why it matters.** Deeptech founders building in AI infrastructure, robotics, and semiconductors have historically faced a capital crunch—most Indian VCs bet on SaaS and fintech returns instead. CortexSpark's fund lowers the barrier to seed and Series A funding for the exact cohort (AI engineers, robotics teams, semiconductor designers) building the foundational layer of India's AI stack. The ₹1,000 crore size signals institutional confidence that deeptech margins and exit multiples justify patient capital.

**Action.** Track CortexSpark's first fund announcements on their website and Crunchbase. Monitor their portfolio for semiconductor and AI chip startups—they will likely be concentrated in Bengaluru and Hyderabad clusters. File the SEBI approval order (search "CortexSpark SEBI approval November 2026") to understand fund size, GP commit, and ticket size.

### Indian AI Startups Raise Record $1.6 Billion Despite Broader Funding Slowdown

A Tracxn report released November 23, 2026 shows Indian AI startups raised $1.6 billion in equity funding during the first nine months of 2026—a sharp jump from the same period last year. The growth was driven by mega-round concentration: a small number of large Series B/C deals commanded most capital, while early-stage and Series A activity remained compressed. Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Chennai accounted for 96 per cent of total AI capital deployed.

**Why it matters.** India's broader startup funding market crashed this quarter (overall VC inflow dropped to $969 million for November), but AI is decoupling. For engineers and founders choosing between generalist and AI-first roles, the data confirms AI is the safest capital bet in 2026 India. The concentration in mega-rounds means early-stage AI consulting, AI agents, and vertical AI SaaS have more competitive pressure—but seed stage AI hiring remains hot because Series B+ rounds are still being cut.

**Action.** Download the full Tracxn AI Funding Report (search "Tracxn Indian AI Startups 2026" on their platform). Cross-reference the mega-round recipients against Y Combinator and 500 Global cohorts to spot which applied research vs. applied product founders got the mega-checks. Monitor CRunchbase "AI" sector tag for Indian companies tracked at $100M+ valuation.

*Sources: [[Telangana Today: AI Startup Funding Report](https://telanganatoday.com/ai-startup-funding-nearly-doubles-d4c9ef10)]([Telangana Today: AI Startup Funding Report](https://telanganatoday.com/ai-startup-funding-nearly-doubles-d4c9ef10)) · [[Tracxn Analytics](https://tracxn.com)]([Tracxn Analytics](https://tracxn.com)) · [[Inc42 Indian Startup News](https://inc42.com/buzz)]([Inc42 Indian Startup News](https://inc42.com/buzz))*

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### TATASTEEL (NSE): -8.43% on ₹28,000cr tubes-and-colour sale to APL Apollo; capex commitment ₹16,756cr

Tata Steel plunged 8.43% to close at ₹163.00 on November 23, dragged by its announcement to divest tubes and colour coated businesses to APL Apollo Tubes Limited for approximately ₹28,000 crore, paired with an open offer to acquire up to 26% additional stake in APL Apollo at ₹2,301.40 per share—a capex pledge of ₹16,756 crore. The stock closed near its day's low, underperforming the broader Nifty Metal index, which fell 3.70% in a market-wide profit-taking session that ended a four-week winning streak. Volume remained elevated as large portfolios rebalanced.

**Why it matters.** The restructuring marks Tata Steel's shift to a pure-play export and specialty-steel play by exiting lower-margin downstream segments—a strategic pivot that telegraphs near-term capex pressure and interim margin pressure. The deal's size (₹28,000cr SOP) and the ₹16,756cr acquisition fund pull capital from domestic expansion at a time when European operations remain under margin compression (per Q2 guidance, coking-coal costs in Europe face upside). Read-across: other conglomerate heavy-capex plays (Larsen & Toubro, Reliance) may face similar valuation scrutiny if sentiment tilts toward cash-generative over growth-capex names. For India-focused investors, this signals that Tata Steel's turnaround now hinges on APL Apollo synergies and export realization, not domestic volume accretion.

**Action.** File the 23 November BSE/NSE announcement and read the scheme structure and Tata Steel's investor call transcript (if published) to gauge management's timeline for integration and cash generation. Watch the ₹155–160 support level on retest; a break below may signal broader conglomerate destocking. Cross-check the Q3 capex guidance revision when FY27 Q3 results land (expected early February 2027). RIC: Tata Steel Limited, scrip code 500470 (NSE), 500470 (BSE).

### TCS (NSE): +3.53% on outperformance as banks and metals bleed

Tata Consultancy Services rose 3.53% to ₹2,460.00 on November 23, the top Nifty 50 gainer in a down market, as defensive IT demand offset a broad sell-off in cyclical sectors. The Sensex fell 1,483.72 points (−1.77%) to 82,435.99, while Nifty Bank plummeted 3.1% and Nifty Metal shed 3.70%; by contrast, TCS held firm, signaling flight-to-quality into large-cap IT amid profit-taking after a four-week rally.

**Why it matters.** TCS's relative strength reflects two currents: (a) foreign investors' record ₹1.12 lakh crore November inflows have favoured large-cap IT over cyclicals, as global capital rotates away from AI-exposed mega-cap tech in the US; (b) India's IT export tailwind (12–15% growth guided for FY27) and 4.71% trailing dividend yield (interim dividend ₹12 per share, announced earlier in October) appeal to yield-hunting foreign allocators. For engineers watching from Hyderabad, this underscores IT's shelter status in downturns—TCS and peers Infosys may outperform if macro uncertainty persists, but mean-reversion risk is real if DII selling (₹2,760cr offloaded 23 Nov) accelerates.

**Action.** Watch TCS's Q2 FY27 earnings release and management commentary on US client capex spend and attrition trends (target: sub-16% gross attrition). The ₹2,500 level is the near-term resistance; a retest of ₹2,350–2,400 would indicate broad-market participation in the rally recovery. Check NSE bulk-deal trackers for any stake build-outs or exits by anchor investors. Next results expected late January 2027 for Q3 FY27.

## 💹 Global Stocks

### NVDA (NASDAQ): +31.48% after Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO, largest single-day market cap gain on record.

Nvidia shares surged 31.48% to $165.05 on Monday, November 23, adding an estimated $952 billion to the company's market value—a record single-day increase. Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO by the board overshadowed last week's post-earnings selloff; the stock had fallen 24% in November and posted six consecutive weekly declines despite beating Q3 earnings. The Nasdaq Composite leaped 6.51% and the S&P 500 rallied 4.73%, their best day since April 2025, with volume surging to 781 million shares.

**Why it matters.** Huang's return reverses two weeks of AI-sector capitulation and signals board confidence in NVDA's AI chip dominance despite near-term governance questions. The rebound sparked a broadside semiconductor rally—the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 14.03%, pulling along ASML (+9.28%), ARM (+16.08%), and Intel (+13%+)—that restores momentum to the mega-cap chip complex which underpins both US cloud capex and global AI infrastructure. For India tech (TCS, Infosys, HCL), the chip strength lifts demand signals for semiconductors-adjacent services, though the rally vindicates positioning in NVDA over geopolitical hedges. The move says governance resolved a founder-CEO risk; market repricing of NVDA's $2.68 non-GAAP EPS beat (vs. $2.47 consensus) and $115.8B revenue (vs. $109.15B) now feels complete.

**Action.** File 8-K at SEC (expected imminently if not filed; check sec.gov for NVIDIA CORP, Central Index Key 1045810). Nvidia earnings transcript from November 17, 2026 available via investor.nvidia.com. Watch $180 and $190 as near-term resistance levels; prior-week low of ~$127 is now major support. Monitor upcoming analyst day calendars and institutional ownership shifts (Form 4 filings for Huang's equity awards).

*Sources: [[Yahoo Finance: Stock market rally Nov 23](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-dow-p-141517672.html)]([Yahoo Finance: Stock market rally Nov 23](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-dow-p-141517672.html)) · [[CNBC: Nvidia earnings report](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q3-2027.html)]([CNBC: Nvidia earnings report](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q3-2027.html)) · [[SEC Edgar: NVIDIA filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000088/q3fy27pr.htm)]([SEC Edgar: NVIDIA filings](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000088/q3fy27pr.htm))*

### 2330.TW (Taiwan Stock Exchange): Taiex +8.99% as TSMC surges +10% (daily limit), leading Asia chipmaker rebound.

Taiwan's Taiex benchmark closed at 40,122.35 on Tuesday, November 24, up 8.99% (3,310 points), after Jensen Huang's reinstatement reignited Asian chip demand. TSMC stock hit its daily 10% limit at the Taiwan Stock Exchange; American depositary receipts had already surged 14.08% in New York on the prior session. The region's recovery follows a 17.5% weekly collapse—Taiwan's steepest drop since 1991—and extends across peers: South Korea's Kospi closed +6.98% at 5,036.99, with Samsung and SK Hynix each climbing 8-10%, while Foxconn added 8-10% and Softbank Group (the mega-cap AI financer) rose over 8%.

**Why it matters.** Huang's return unblocks Taiwan's chip supply chain narrative—TSMC is the foundational supplier to NVDA, AMD, and ARM. A 9%+ rally recapitalizes Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem after five straight weekly losses and validates that geopolitical risk (US export curbs on advanced chips to China) hasn't fundamentally broken the AI cycle. South Korea's resilience (Samsung, SK Hynix both +8%+) shows memory/foundry exposure across the tier-one base. Hong Kong and mainland China lagged sharply (CSI 300 +0.4%, Hang Seng dipped), signaling China remains locked out of the rally despite being TSMC's largest customer—a read on US export controls tightening. TSMC's daily limit hit on 10% suggests supply-chain bottom formation; closing price will determine if buyers are rotating into the name or if circuit-breaker halts cap the move.

**Action.** Monitor TSMC (2330.TW) opening price on Wednesday, November 25; daily limits may lift with fresh sessions. File Form 20-F annual report due March 31, 2027 (last 20-F at sec.gov). Watch for joint analyst updates from Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley on foundry utilization and 2027 capex guidance. Check US Department of Commerce export control schedules (via commerce.gov) for any chips-to-China rule changes that would affect TSMC's customer list.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in $43.9 billion all-stock deal, expanding cloud security footprint

CrowdStrike Holdings announced November 23 a definitive agreement to acquire cloud security leader Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valuing Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion. Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike common shares for each Zscaler share. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028 (ending January 31, 2028), subject to customary closing conditions and Zscaler shareholder approval, and immediately extends CrowdStrike's customer access to roughly 8,000 Zscaler clients not yet on its Falcon platform.

**Why it matters.** This is a core-plus-tuck acquisition by a platform consolidator, not a defensive move. CrowdStrike already dominates endpoint security; it is buying Zscaler's Zero Trust Network Access capability and customer relationships to build a fuller cloud security stack without engineering from scratch. For founders building point solutions in security infrastructure, the signal is stark: distribution and native integration into a larger platform ecosystem matter as much as technology differentiation. Pure-play security vendors face a choice between staying independent (and fighting for mindshare in a world of consolidated buyers) or timing an exit before the buyer can build the feature internally.

**Action.** Founders tracking this space should monitor the regulatory timeline—FTC scrutiny of tech consolidation is real, and a $44 billion deal in security will draw antitrust questions. For operators, watch CrowdStrike's investor calls for how the company bridges Zscaler's standalone ARR into the Falcon installed base. The exchange ratio (1.135) gives you a valuation anchor for other security M&A.

### Ex-Infosys executives launch ₹1,000 crore deeptech fund, expanding India's engineering-first capital

CortexSpark Ventures, founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, announced November 24 the debut of Viksit Bharat Fund-I, a ₹1,000 crore ($120 million) fund targeting deeptech and AI startups in India. The fund holds a ₹400 crore greenshoe option that could raise total corpus to ₹1,400 crore ($170 million), with plans to deploy capital across approximately 20 portfolio companies in semiconductors, robotics, biotech, and hardware-first sectors.

**Why it matters.** Operator-led funding is gaining traction in Indian deeptech as LPs recognize that founders building hardware, semiconductors, and physics-based companies need more than capital—they need supply chain expertise, enterprise customer access, and patience with longer engineering timelines. Infosys alumni bring direct relationships to enterprise customers in infrastructure and manufacturing, unblocking go-to-market challenges that typical VC firms cannot solve. This fund joins Oister Global's ₹600 crore growth fund and reported ₹700 crore raises from Unacademy co-founders, signaling a cluster of experienced capital flowing into India's deeptech gap.

**Action.** Deeptech founders in India should map which Infosys business units (consulting, cloud, BPO, digital) the fund's LPs worked with; that history often predicts portfolio concentration and enterprise TAM assumptions. Watch CortexSpark's first announcements (expect portfolio reveals in Q1 2027) to identify sector focus. For enterprise and infrastructure builders, understanding which funds are staffed by operator-founders with specific customer relationships is as critical as fund size.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### Leukemia's 50-Year Origin Story — Cambridge Study Shows AML Begins Decades Before Diagnosis

Researchers from the University of Cambridge and UCL analyzed 47 women who developed acute myeloid leukemia using annual blood samples, some collected up to 15 years before diagnosis, combined with ultra-sensitive DNA sequencing and mathematical modeling. The study, published in Nature on November 11, 2026, found that the first cancer-driving mutation appeared before age 20 in approximately two-thirds of cases—more than 50 years before the typical age of diagnosis.

**Why it matters.** This work rewrites the AML timeline from an acute disease to a process spanning decades. Each successive mutation roughly doubled to tripled the growth rate of affected cells, with cells carrying four driver mutations doubling in a matter of weeks. The implication is actionable: even a small reduction in clone growth rate over a decade-plus window between early mutations and diagnosis could meaningfully lower leukemia risk, opening the door to preventive therapies in high-risk populations. For AI-builders in oncology, this validates the case for retrospective analysis of biobanked blood samples to identify actionable preleukemic states.

**Action.** The Cambridge team plans to identify which high-risk clones are most likely to progress and whether early intervention—potentially immunotherapy or small-molecule growth inhibitors—can safely prevent transformation. Investigators interested in preleukemic monitoring should read the Nature article for the mathematical model of clone dynamics; the ASCO Post summary captures the clinical interpretation. High-impact next step: prospective trials in people with detectable preleukemic mutations matched for age and clone burden.

### AI Spots Bladder Cancer Years Before Diagnosis — 85% Detection Rate in 70,000-Patient Welsh Health Records

Researchers at the University of Plymouth developed PRECISE-AGZ, a machine-learning model trained on nearly 70,000 patient records collected between 1995 and 2020 from Welsh health databases. The model, published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, achieved 85% sensitivity for detecting bladder cancer cases and 91% specificity for ruling out cancer in unaffected patients, with reliable detection up to 12 months before clinical diagnosis and detectable signals emerging as early as five years beforehand.

**Why it matters.** This is the first EHR-only bladder cancer detection system to outperform National Health Service referral guidelines. It flagged cases using routine clinical data—symptoms, comorbidities, medication use, lifestyle factors—without specialized imaging or invasive procedures. For health systems, it offers a scalable triaging tool to reduce diagnostic delay; for AI builders, it validates that retrospective EHR cohorts can generate clinically actionable predictive signals in solid tumors at scale. Bladder cancer incidence is rising in older populations, and earlier detection improves surgical outcomes.

**Action.** Read the IEEE paper for the feature engineering and class-imbalance handling; Hospimedica's summary outlines the clinical workflow. The model would not replace cystoscopy (which remains diagnostic), but could flag high-risk cases for expedited referral. Health systems should pilot PRECISE-AGZ on prospective primary-care cohorts to validate the five-year window; pharma and diagnostics firms should assess whether this approach generalizes to other urologic or hematologic malignancies.
